phase_name: Land the Anchor-Pointer Convention, Its Regression Lint, and a Pilot

objectives.description: Add the anchor-pointer convention standard under context/standards/
Write the inventory-driven regression lint (reads a permanent collapsed-block registry, not a hardcoded block list)
Decide and record whether the lint gets a new gate row or rides an existing gate
Write the lint's fixture suite with a deliberately-violating fixture plus conforming fixtures
Pilot the collapse on five files drawn from the inventory's highest sharing-factor eligible block, with a claim-retention ledger entry per file
Run the full gate set over the pilot and confirm the finding set matches the Phase 1 baseline; record the phase's NET-MD delta

approaches_tried.approach: grep -Fqz -- "$pattern" "$file" for multi-line literal block containment
approaches_tried.reason: grep -F splits a multi-line PATTERN argument into one alternative pattern PER LINE and reports a match if ANY single line matches anywhere in the target (-z only changes how the INPUT is record-split, never how the PATTERN argument is split) -- it is an OR of single lines, not a contiguous multi-line substring test. Discovered when the real pilot run against the live repo reported all 5 correctly-collapsed files as violations: their removed block's generic lines (```bash, ```json, bare { or }) trivially recur elsewhere in the same file. Replaced with bash's own [[ "$content" == *"$pattern"* ]] (quoted expansion disables glob interpretation), confirmed correct against the real repo (0 violations on the 5 correctly-collapsed files) and against a deliberately-reverted scratch copy (fires on exactly the reverted file, silent on the other 4).
